news.title: Deep dish completes first Pig Trail crossing without spilling
news.text: A 12-inch Chicago-style pie has crossed the Pig Trail from the river valley to Fayetteville with every layer intact. Witnesses credit the crust walls, which were built to Chicago building code and have never once heard of a switchback. The pie arrived at a tailgate, asked for a fork, and was told this is Arkansas, everybody has a fork.

faq.question: Is Windy Holler a real restaurant?
faq.answer: No. Windy Holler is a parody pizzeria. Every name, address, phone number, dish, price, and story here is invented, and it is not affiliated with any real restaurant or with the University of Arkansas.

faq.question: When are you open?
faq.answer: On paper: 11 am–10 pm Monday through Thursday, 11 am–midnight Friday and Saturday, and noon–9 pm Sunday. In practice, never. We are fictional.

faq.question: What is tavern cut?
faq.answer: Thin crust cut into squares instead of wedges, the way Chicago bars have long served it. The corner pieces are the prize.

faq.question: Is Chicago-style deep dish a casserole?
faq.answer: It is a pizza that has made some bold life choices. Every pizza here comes deep dish or tavern-cut thin, so you can pick your side of the argument.

faq.question: Do I really need a fork for the deep dish?
faq.answer: You don't need one. You'll want one. A knife helps too.

faq.question: Can I book a room for a party?
faq.answer: Fayetteville has the Bleacher Room and Rogers has the Upper Deck. Both are fictional, so they are always available and never bookable.

faq.question: When is trivia night?
faq.answer: Fayetteville on Wednesdays, Bentonville on Tuesdays, and Texarkana on Thursdays, in both states.
